text:
Maria: Quick heads-up — ran the FA v3 probe across the staged fleet this morning. high-level summary first: seq512 p50 improved ~12ms, p99 shifted +3ms in a few narrow cases where KV miss spikes. overall cost per-token down ~1.6%.

Chen: nice. which workloads did you run?

Maria: mixed: chat (avg seq 256), long-form generation (seq 1024), and a synthetic seq512/768 microbench for kernel handoff. used batching profile 'prod-default' and toggled attn.use_flash_v3 on the kernel chooser.

Albert: can you paste the profiler output for the seq512 run?

Maria: sure — paste below. note: trimmed for slack.

```
# seq512 synthetic, 8k tokens total across batch
flash_v3 kernel: avg token ms = 0.89
legacy fa2: avg token ms = 1.01
kv miss rate (page faults): 0.7% -> 3.2% during tail spikes
p50 latency: 24ms -> 12ms
p99 latency: 110ms -> 113ms
CPU util on host: +6% (kernel CPU path for kv eviction)
```

Devon: that KV miss spike is the thing to watch. does it correlate with batching windows?

Maria: yep — when batch size jumps to >64 with hot-prefix churn, we see more page evictions and KV cache thrashing. looks like Flash v3's paged attention path is touching the cache differently than v2.

Chen: did you try adjusting the minibatch trigger and max_batch?

Maria: ran two quick knobs: lowered max_batch from 256 -> 128 and tightened batch_timeout by 15ms. p99 regressions disappeared in the long-form run, p50 improvement persisted. cost delta still ~1.3%.

Tim: so conservative rollout plan: 1) internal canary (api-stage) with attn.use_flash_v3=false by default, enable for 5% of traffic routed by kernel-chooser policy; 2) monitor p50/p95/p99, KV miss rate, gpu mem_pressure, and cpu steal; 3) if p99 delta > +10ms or KV miss rate > 5% trigger rollback. sound right?

Albert: add token-cost-per-second and request-failure-rate. Also add a latent QA check: run eval prompt set A every 30m and verify top-k sampling outputs don't regress (we had a sample drift in previous rollout).

Chen: feature flag names + gating: attn.use_flash_v3 (global), attn.force_paged_kv (opt-in), attn.batch_timeout_ms_override (runtime override). We'll expose these to canary service and console.

Maria: ops-bot shows the smoke run succeeded on api-stage: ops-bot: deploy/3366007800 finished, canary enabled -> 5% traffic.

ops-bot: monitor: p50=18ms (-11), p99=115ms (+1), kv_miss_rate=2.8%, error_rate=0.02% :eyes:

Devon: runbook item — if kv_miss_rate ticks over 4% for two consecutive 5m windows, disable attn.force_paged_kv and drop max_batch to 128 automatically. I'll add a step to the autoscaler playbook.

Chen: question on rollout sequencing — prefer region-by-region (us-west -> us-east -> eu) or by customer-tier? Some enterprise tenants are on dedicated pools.

Tim: do region-by-region for hosted API first, dedicated pools we treat as manual opt-in. document gating metrics in the console and signal to SEs.

Maria: small regression note: in one long-form run we saw transient +8ms on p99 when kv eviction GC kicked in — root cause appears to be GC running inline in the CUDA path for paged KV. need to investigate kernel yield points.

Albert: action: I'll profile with nvprof and `cupti` to get kernel timelines and check for sync points. target: identify whether we can defer GC out-of-band to avoid tail spikes.

Devon: also split tests for sequence shapes: short-chat (seq<128), medium (256-512), long (>=1024). each needs separate gating thresholds (p99 budget differs).

Maria: agreed. I'll add baseline numbers to the integration doc and create a checklist for rollout:
- confirm kernel chooser fallback: attn.chooser_order includes [flash_v3, flash_v2, paged_fallback]
- add feature flags in console with rollout slider
- create canary monitors (p50/p95/p99, kv_miss_rate, token_cost, cpu/gpu util)
- automated rollback triggers (kv_miss >4%, p99 > +10ms, error_rate >0.5%)
- staged regions and dedicated opt-in plan
- QA evals run at 30m cadence

Chen: please also include a short communication blurb for support/SEs explaining expected perf deltas and how to opt-out.

Maria: will do. I'll push the playbook to the infra repo under: infra/runbooks/attn/flashv3-rollout.md and link from console.

Tim: any outstanding blockers?

Maria: two: Albert needs a few more profiler runs to propose a GC mitigation, and ops wants a safety hook to throttle batch sizes automatically on KV pressure. both on the critical path for broad rollout.

Albert: on it — will drop results by EOD.

Devon: I'll draft the metric alert rules and add them to the runbook.

Maria: perfect. thanks team :rocket:
